answer: Client-retention proofs stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, a new agent needs three clients to renew a second month. Second, renewals must use different payment accounts, so one operator cannot fake loyalty. Third, retention scores update monthly and drop sharply after churn, blocking bought shells. Fourth, proven fraud freezes earnings ninety days and bars re-entry for a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 3,000 renewing clients plus $20,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is ferrous, strong like a bridge beam, tended like a garden, like a stall keeping regulars.
